chapter: Own bands and Los Angeles clubs
title: The intimate Oasis combo with Par Jones, Ernie Freeman, Maxwell Davis
summary: At the Oasis Lee used trumpet with a hat or mute, tenor, piano, brushes and bass so patrons could talk and dance.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah, he was kind of a character. And he worked with me at the Downbeat, too. Because, you know, I remember that he worked with me about 2 or 3 different places, but after we went to the -- had a real great trumpet player at The Oasis; his name was Par Jones. I don't know, did you know Par Jones?
Uh huh.

Par Jones used to put that harmon mute in there, and the Oasis was an intimate place, and I just used tenor, trumpet, piano, drums and bass. And I made him play with a hat over the bell of his horn or with the horn in mute, you know, and I used brushes all the time, and the people just -- you know, you had to play for people to dance, and the people had to talk, and they could hear themselves. And we stayed there quite some time, you know?
How long?
A couple of years we stayed there.
Who was your piano player?
At that time ... you won't believe it.
Ernie Freeman.
Oh?
Uh huh. Ernie Freeman. And Maxwell Davis was the tenor saxophone player. But it was Ernie Freeman.
And The Oasis was at 38th and Western?
And Western Avenue, yeah.
In fact, it was about the only jazz club we had then, wasn't it? After the Empire Club closed and the Cotton Club moved to Hollywood, and the Alabam was still operating, though.
Yeah, the Alabam was still operating.
But there really wasn't much jazz; it was -- well, part of the time. I think Hampton played there once.
Yeah, he did. Yeah. I'm thinking now from the time of the Oasis ...
The Cricket Club.
Yeah, The Cricket Club. I don't know if I remember the Cricket Club. Two years later, after I left The Oasis, in '53 I joined Nat. You know, I think I'll take it up to that.
Was there anything of significance between The Oasis and Nat?
No, that seems to be a blank. If I can think of it, I'll let you know, but I don't know; that's why I didn't want to fool with the years, you know? Because some-
thing has got to get lost in there, you know? Well, the thing that helped me was finding this '43 and '42. But I'll take it from, going in to joining Nat ...
